examples.en: Let me introduce myself first.
I introduced myself in the first class.
This book has a short introduction.
I want to read the company introduction.

explain: ‘소개해요’는 사람, 가게, 책 모두에 써요. 소개를 받으면 ‘소개받았어요’라고 해요.

phrases.en: a blind date set up by a friend
phrases.nuance_ko: 아는 사람이 연애 상대를 소개해 줘서 처음 만나는 자리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: a first meeting where an acquaintance introduces you to a possible romantic partner
phrases.en_equiv: a blind date set up by a friend

dict_examples.ko: 두 사람은 김 선생의 소개로 만났습니다.
dict_examples.en: The two of them met through Mr. Kim's introduction.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: ‘소개해요’ works for people, shops, and books. When you are introduced to someone, you say ‘소개받았어요’.

examples.en: I study Spanish.
It's Spanish.
Spanish class is on Monday.
My younger sibling is learning Spanish.
In Mexico they use Spanish.
Do you speak Spanish well?

explain: 스페인 + 어 = 스페인어. 멕시코나 아르헨티나 사람도 스페인어를 쓰지만 '멕시코어'라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.nuance_en: For learning a language, you say 'study + language-object'.
Adding 로 shows which language you use.

phrases.nuance_ko: '스페인어' 뒤에 명사를 붙여 '스페인어로 된 것'을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a noun after 스페인어 to mean something in Spanish.

explain_en: 스페인 + 어 = Spanish. People in Mexico or Argentina speak Spanish too, but nobody says '멕시코어'.

examples.en: I study French.
Is it French?
I don't know French.
That person is a French teacher.
This song is a French song.
French is a little difficult.

explain: 프랑스 + 어 = 프랑스어. 옛날 말로 '불어'라고도 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '프랑스어'의 옛날 말이에요. 요즘은 '프랑스어'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An older word for 프랑스어; 프랑스어 is more common today.
For learning a language, you say 'study + language-object'.
Adding 로 shows which language you use.

explain_en: 프랑스 + 어 = French. An older word for it is 불어.

examples.en: I clean my room on the weekend.

examples.ko: 내일 손님이 와요. 오늘 집 청소가 필요해요.
examples.en: Guests are coming tomorrow. The house needs cleaning today.
Who does the cleaning? — I do.
I clean every Saturday.

explain: 물건을 제자리에 놓는 건 ‘정리’, 바닥을 닦고 쓰는 건 ‘청소’예요. ‘방 정리’와 ‘방 청소’는 달라요.

phrases.en: I clean the house on Saturday.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter way to say 청소를 해요.
Use it when cleaning is done.
Adding 좀 makes the request softer.

dict_examples.en: The house had been cleaned spotless.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Putting things back in their place is ‘정리’; wiping and sweeping the floor is ‘청소’. ‘방 정리’ and ‘방 청소’ are different.

examples.ko: 할머니와 식사할 때는 먼저 수저를 들지 않아요.
examples.en: When eating with my grandmother, I don't pick up my spoon and chopsticks first.
After finishing the meal, I put my spoon and chopsticks down on the table.
Could you set out the spoons and chopsticks?

examples.ko: 컵은 챙겼어요. 그런데 수저는 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: I packed a cup. But I left the spoon and chopsticks behind.
I'm teaching my child how to use a spoon and chopsticks.

explain: '숟가락'과 '젓가락'을 합친 말이라 한 벌로 묶어서 '수저 한 벌'이라고 세요. 식탁에 놓을 때는 '수저를 놓다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저 친구는 금수저예요. 집이 아주 부자예요.
phrases.en: That friend is a 'gold spoon'. His family is very rich.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부잣집에서 태어난 사람을 가리키는 말이에요. 반대는 '흙수저'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone born into a rich family. The opposite is '흙수저' (dirt spoon).

explain_en: It combines '숟가락' (spoon) and '젓가락' (chopsticks), so a set is counted as '수저 한 벌'. Laying them on the table is '수저를 놓다'.

examples.en: I had a meeting, so I couldn't answer the phone.
The office phone keeps ringing.
What is your friend's phone number?
I'm working now. Please call me later.
I got a call from my mom.

explain: 전화번호는 숫자를 하나씩 읽어요. 0은 보통 ‘공’이라고 해요. 010은 ‘공일공’이에요.

phrases.example: 식당에 전화 넣어서 자리가 있는지 물어볼게요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 회사 같은 곳에 볼일이 있어서 전화할 때 쓰는 입말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: colloquial; used when you call a shop or company because you have business there

dict_examples.ko: 일주일 동안 전화 한 통 없다.
dict_examples.en: Not a single call in a whole week.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Your teacher called a little while ago.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 주말마다 전화로 부모님께 안부를 전한다.
dict_examples.en: Every weekend he calls his parents to see how they're doing.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 제가 경찰에 실종 신고를 내기 전에 저한테 전화를 주시기 바랍니다.
dict_examples.en: Please call me before I report you missing to the police.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Read phone numbers one digit at a time. 0 is usually read as ‘공’. 010 is ‘공일공’.

dis.h: a phone call; the act of calling

p.n: 전화기 is the device, so 전화기를 하다 makes no sense.

t90.ax: I got a call from my mom.

en: to ripen; to be cooked through

examples.en: The persimmons have ripened to a deep red.

examples.ko: 고기가 아직 안 익어서 더 구워야 해요.
examples.en: The meat isn't cooked through yet, so we have to grill it more.
The kimchi has fermented well and tastes great.
Wait a little until the ramen is cooked.
Let's eat the sweet potatoes together when they're cooked.
The tomatoes aren't ripe yet, so they're hard.

explain: 과일이나 음식이 다 되었을 때 쓰고, 반대는 '설익다'나 '덜 익다'예요. 김치가 시간이 지나 맛이 드는 것도 '익다'라고 해요. 남이 익게 하는 것은 '익히다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 길이 눈에 익어요. 전에 와 본 것 같아요.
phrases.en: This road looks familiar. I think I've been here before.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 봐서 낯설지 않다는 뜻이에요. '손에 익다'는 자주 해서 일이 편해졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means something no longer feels strange because you have seen it often. '손에 익다' means a task has become easy through repetition.

explain_en: It is used when fruit or food has fully ripened or cooked; the opposite is '설익다' or '덜 익다'. It is also used when kimchi develops flavor over time. Making something cook is '익히다'.

t90.ax: Wait a little until the ramen is cooked.

examples.en: I drive to work every day.
Sorry. Could you drive for us?
Don't drive when you're sleepy.
My father listens to music when he drives.
When my older brother drives, I sit beside him.

examples.ko: 저는 운전할 수 있어요. 면허가 있어요.
examples.en: I can drive. I have a license.

explain: 차를 직접 모는 것이고 '차를 몰다'라고도 해요. 타고 가기만 하는 것은 '타다'라서 구별해요. '운전을 하다'처럼 사이를 띄워도 쓰고, '운전석', '운전면허'처럼 다른 말과도 자주 붙어요.

phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 'unjeonhada', same meaning.
The polite form; it can also link as '운전해서 가요'.

phrases.en: I got my driver's license last year.
phrases.nuance_en: The license that lets you drive.

explain_en: It means operating a vehicle yourself, and '차를 몰다' is another way to say it. Simply riding is '타다', so keep them apart. It can be split as '운전을 하다' and often forms compounds like '운전석' (driver's seat) and '운전면허' (driver's license).

t90.ax: I drive to work every day.

examples.en: I study hard.
I study at the library.

examples.ko: 내일 시험이에요. 오늘 공부를 많이 할 거예요.
examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow. I'll study a lot today.
Studying Korean is fun.
Where do you study? — I study at home.

explain: ‘공부를 잘해요’는 성적이 좋다는 뜻이에요. 공부하는 방법이 아니라 결과를 말해요.

phrases.example: 이번 실수가 저한테 좋은 공부가 됐어요.
phrases.en: to be a good lesson; a learning experience
phrases.nuance_ko: 책 공부가 아니라 경험에서 무언가를 배웠을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when you learned something from experience, not from a book
phrases.en_equiv: to be a good lesson; a learning experience

explain_en: ‘공부를 잘해요’ means someone gets good grades. It describes the result, not how they study.

examples.en: On rainy days I think of kimchi pancakes.
If you add onion to the kimchi pancake, it gets sweeter.

examples.ko: 우리 김치전 한 장 더 시킬까요?
examples.en: Shall we order one more kimchi pancake?
I had a kimchi pancake together with bean sprout soup.

explain: 김치를 넣어 얇게 부친 음식이에요. 만들 때는 '굽다'보다 '부치다'를 써서 '전을 부치다'라고 해요. '김치부침개'도 같은 음식을 가리키는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I made kimchi pancakes with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_en: Remember that pancakes like this use '부치다', not '굽다'.

phrases.en: My mom made kimchi pancakes for me.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same dish as '김치전'.

phrases.en: I dip the kimchi pancake in soy sauce and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 방법을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase describing how the dish is eaten.
phrases.en_equiv: to dip kimchi pancake in soy sauce

explain_en: It is a thin pancake pan-fried with kimchi. When making it, you say '전을 부치다' rather than '굽다'. '김치부침개' is another name for the same dish.

examples.en: I fell asleep watching TV in the living room.
Our TV suddenly turned off.
I heard today's weather news on TV.

examples.ko: 티브이는 밥 먹을 때 끄는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to turn the TV off when eating.

examples.ko: 새 티브이로 바꿨더니 화면이 훨씬 선명해요.
examples.en: I switched to a new TV and the picture is much clearer.

explain: '텔레비전'을 줄여 한글로 쓴 말로, 영어 TV를 읽은 소리예요. 말할 때는 '티비'라고도 많이 하는데, 글에서는 '티브이'나 'TV'로 써요. '티브이를 보다/켜다/끄다'처럼 함께 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 많이 쓰는 형태이고, 글에서는 '티브이'나 'TV'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common spoken form; in writing use '티브이' or 'TV'.

phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이지 않은 원래 말로, 조금 더 격식 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened word, a bit more formal.

phrases.en: When I get home, I turn on the TV first.
phrases.nuance_en: Good to learn together with '끄다' (turn off).

explain_en: It is the Hangul spelling of the sound of English 'TV', short for '텔레비전'. In speech people often say '티비', but in writing it is '티브이' or 'TV'. It pairs with verbs as in '티브이를 보다/켜다/끄다'.
